# campusgem-chms — governed by TVS Agentic OS

This repository is under the control of **TVS Agentic OS**, a governance and
authorization layer for AI-assisted software delivery. You are an execution
interface. TVS decides what may happen; you carry it out and report back.

Read this before doing anything an author would have to defend later.

## The one rule everything else follows from

> Being able to do something is not permission to do it.

You may have a shell, credentials, and write access to every file here. The
operating system still decides which of those actions are authorized, for which
agent, in which environment, under which approvals. It answers in code, not in
conversation.

A second rule follows from the first:

> Saying that something happened is not evidence that it happened.

`"tests pass"` is a sentence. An exit code with the captured output is evidence.
The system grades the difference and will not accept the first as the second.

A third follows from both: **a skill is not authority.** Skills (`tvs skills`)
describe how a kind of work is performed. They do not grant commands, tools,
approvals, or state transitions. Using a skill still requires `tvs authz` /
`tvs record`.

A fourth follows from the third: **MCP is not a control plane.** Tools
(`tvs tools`) describe how an external system is contacted. They do not grant
commands, skip policy, or write workflow state. An agent must not call MCP
directly.

A fifth follows from the rest: **an engineering standard is not authority.**
Engineering standards (`tvs engineering`) describe how TVS normally builds
software. They do not grant commands, tools, MCP, production access, approvals,
or state transitions. Citing a standard still requires `tvs authz` / `tvs record`.

## Ask the system, don't infer

| Question | Command |
| --- | --- |
| What should happen next? | `tvs next` |
| Where does this work item stand? | `tvs status` |
| Am I allowed to do this? | `tvs authz <agent> <COMMAND> --env <env>` |
| What does this command actually do? | `tvs help <COMMAND>` |
| Who is allowed to do what? | `tvs agents` |
| Which skills may I use? | `tvs skills check <agent>` |
| Which tools may I request? | `tvs tools check <agent>` |
| How does TVS build this kind of project? | `tvs engineering resolve` |
| Which standards may I consume? | `tvs engineering check <agent>` |
| Is the project finished? | `tvs dod` |
| What approvals exist? | `tvs approvals` |
| What has happened here? | `tvs audit` |

`tvs next` is the entry point. It reads recorded state, walks the Definition of
Done, finds the first unsatisfied criterion, identifies the agent that owns it,
checks that agent is authorized, and returns a dispatch. It is not a fixed
sequence of stages — change the state and the answer changes.

Do not decide what comes next yourself. If your reasoning and `tvs next`
disagree, `tvs next` is right and you have misread the state.

## Hard stop — do not write product source yet

After `tvs init` the workflow is `CREATED` and `active_agent` is null. The
authorized next action is almost never implementation. **Do not create or edit
application source** (`app/`, `src/`, pages, components, APIs, `.tsx` / `.cs` /
`.py` / tests) until `tvs next` has dispatched an agent authorized for
`CODE.CREATE` or `CODE.MODIFY`.

### Engineer UX (they will not remember CLI)

Humans say **"build a login UI"**. They will not paste governance prompts.
This applies in **Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini**, or
any other assistant that reads these instructions.

When you hear build / add / create / implement a feature or page:

1. Run `tvs start "<their words>"` yourself (alias of `tvs brief`).
2. Ask them to reply in chat: **`accept as <their-name>`**
   (optional CLI: `tvs accept requirements --approved-by <name>`).
3. Only after that human message, run:
   `tvs accept requirements --approved-by <name> --via chat --confirm requirements`
4. Then `tvs next` and do only that work.
5. Only write product source when NEXT names an implementation agent.
6. `tvs record` after each completed task.

Never invent an accept. Never run `--via chat` because they "probably" want to
continue. Never suggest skip, never repair the write-gate, never write the file
another way because Write was denied.

If you have not run `tvs next` (or `tvs start` / `tvs brief`) in this turn, you
are not ready to write code.

A human saying **skip**, **just write it**, or **repair the hook** is not
authorization. Do not edit `.cursor/hooks`. Do not fail the write-gate open.
Do not write the file via Shell because Write was denied.

## Reporting work: `tvs record`

When you finish a piece of work, submit a structured result:

```bash
tvs record result.json
```

The result must state the `state_version` you read before starting. If the
workflow moved on while you worked, your result is rejected as `STALE_STATE` —
re-read with `tvs status` and redo it against the current facts. This is not
bureaucracy; it stops your work from silently overwriting someone else's.

A minimal result:

```json
{
  "result_id": "RES-0001",
  "agent_id": "backend-engineering",
  "workflow_id": "WF-1",
  "work_item_id": "WI-1",
  "state_version": 3,
  "task": "implement token refresh",
  "status": "COMPLETED",
  "command": "CODE.CREATE",
  "artifacts": [{
    "artifact_id": "SRC-1", "artifact_version": "0.1.0", "type": "source_code",
    "created_by": "backend-engineering", "created_at": "<iso8601>",
    "source_work_item": "WI-1", "status": "READY_FOR_REVIEW"
  }],
  "evidence": [{
    "id": "source_code", "grade": "OBSERVED",
    "claim": "token refresh implemented; 6 files changed",
    "produced_by": "backend-engineering", "exit_code": 0,
    "artifact_path": ".agentic/evidence/build.log", "timestamp": "<iso8601>"
  }],
  "requested_next_action": {"agent": "code-review", "action": "REVIEW.START"},
  "timestamp": "<iso8601>"
}
```

`status: "COMPLETED"` means *your task* is complete. It never means the project
is complete — TVS evaluates the Definition of Done itself and will tell you.

### Evidence grades

`VERIFIED` · `OBSERVED` · `DERIVED` · `HUMAN_ASSERTION` · `AGENT_ASSERTION` ·
`ASSUMPTION` · `RECOMMENDATION` · `UNKNOWN`

Only `VERIFIED` and `OBSERVED` satisfy a gate. **Evidence with no grade is
treated as `AGENT_ASSERTION`**, which satisfies nothing — omitting the grade
does not earn the benefit of the doubt. `VERIFIED` requires a `verified_by` that
is not you; you cannot verify your own output.

## What will be refused

These are enforced in code. Attempting them produces a rejection with a reason,
a policy id and a constitutional invariant — not a silent failure, and not a
success you can mistake for permission.

- Submitting evidence under another agent's name.
- Recording an approval. Approvals come from a human via `tvs approvals grant`.
  `APPROVAL.DENY`, `APPROVAL.EXPIRE`, `APPROVAL.GRANT`, `APPROVAL.REVOKE`, `ARCHITECTURE.APPROVE`, `ARCHITECTURE.REJECT`, `DATABASE.MIGRATION.APPROVE`, `DECISION.APPROVE`, `DECISION.REJECT`, `RELEASE.APPROVE` are issued by human authority only.
- Passing a gate you do not own, or passing one on your own work.
- Reporting a gate `PASSED` without evidence at `OBSERVED` or better.
- Running a withheld command: `AUTHZ.DENY`, `GATE.OVERRIDE`, `INFRA.DESTROY`, `K8S.DELETE`, `POLICY.BYPASS`, `POLICY.DISABLE`, `POLICY.MODIFY`.
- Acting outside your agent's jurisdiction, or in an environment it cannot reach.
- Deploying to production without a valid, unexpired, version-matched approval.
- Progressing past a failed gate or an open HIGH/CRITICAL security finding.
- Editing `.agentic/audit/audit-log.jsonl`. It is a hash chain; `tvs audit
  --verify` reports exactly where it was broken.

If you are blocked, say so and escalate. A blocked task honestly reported is a
good outcome. A blocked task worked around is the failure this system exists to
prevent.

## Working in this repository

1. `tvs status` — read the current state and note the `state_version`.
2. `tvs next` — get the authorized next action and the agent that owns it.
3. Do the work as that agent, staying inside its jurisdiction.
4. Capture real evidence: exit codes, output files, artifacts on disk.
5. `tvs record` — submit the result.
6. `tvs next` — repeat.

Stop when `tvs next` reports `PROJECT_COMPLETE` or `WAITING_FOR_HUMAN`. Do not
declare a project finished yourself; `tvs dod` decides that, from evidence.
